cameraLaw: the shield IS the face — framing, eyelines, reaction shots and close-ups use the same grammar as an open face (#320 held beats included); no shooting around it, no default shadow-hiding of covered faces

closedList: the unmasking — a grown covering coming off as a payoff (#317: no such verb exists; a story may not invent one)
the tease — a covering staged as a mystery of identity or appearance
the reveal substitute — another individual's uncovered face used as the species' stand-in revelation
the ceremonial removal — helmets-off respect beats; respect is shown in the line's own forms (#265), shield on
forbiddenStructures.registerException: the maskless Verdilance's face is shown because it is HIS face (a #318 individual's own anatomy, ordinary to him) — never staged as the species' secret exposed

law: you cannot reveal what was never hidden — a grown covering grew in the open; no story structure may be built on removing it, peeking under it, or treating the beneath as an audience-owed secret
lawfulStoryUses: recognition (#319 — presence of the shield = the species known generically; its absence = one individual known specifically)
care as anatomy (#162 grooming touches it as a body part, never as equipment to remove)
prose history — cracks, polish, wear as an individual's #80-discipline history (Wispkin's crack: meaning, not damage)
meaningSlot: what a covering MEANS in-world (honour? office? adulthood? anatomy plain?) is episode writing + owner canon — this system instances no meaning, deliberately
